ranked_facts.why: The presence of an early diastolic blowing decrescendo murmur is more characteristic of aortic regurgitation than aortic stenosis, as it indicates blood flowing back into the left ventricle during diastole, a hallmark of aortic regurgitation.
Bounding pulses are a classic sign of aortic regurgitation due to the increased stroke volume and subsequent wide pulse pressure, which is not typically seen in aortic stenosis.
